name: The Reclamation of the Library
title: The Reclamation of the Library, the Cook Who Poisons the Garden, and the Circle That Went Nowhere
era: Raventree Crisis — Feyward Operations / The Library Reclamation / Kitchen Contact
location: The Overgrown Manor - the library reading floor, the polished hallways, the mushroom room, the kitchen, an upstairs bathroom, and a one-being-wide passage that goes in a circle
type: Feyward Room Clearance / Kitchen Contact / Party Fracture
summary: Hjumpik was reading his own Waluipedia dossier when he looked left and saw a shambling mound eating the library. He abandoned the standing order to go upstairs, set a marching order with a battered fairy at the front, and took the room back - killing a creature that was most of the way dead already. What followed was a corridor with polished marble, a cook who has been poisoning the overgrowth by feeding it, a guard who spent twenty minutes protecting a plant with no face, a violet fungus in a toilet, and a secret passage that let everybody out exactly where they went in. The session ends with Waluigi and Hjumpik arguing about whether any of it counted - the dwarf arguing they cannot fight every battle, the archivist arguing the plants are weak enough to take - and with Waluigi reaching past Hjumpik's hand to open a door on something that is not half dead at all.
description: Waluigi is filing this one with an unusual problem, which is that he is in it. Not at the edge of it taking notes - in it, arguing, at volume, in a corridor, about whether this party has accomplished anything in the Overgrown Manor at all. The session began with the single most flattering thing that has ever happened to this archive: Hjumpik Deldkur, sober and unprompted, reading volume eleven of Waluipedia with his finger under the line. It ends with Waluigi admitting out loud, over the roar of something enormous, that he can no longer afford not to care. In between: a library defended for its own sake, an overkill dressed as a victory, a Toad who could not say what had just happened to him, a kitchen commander running the best strategy in the house out of a stockpot, and a hidden passage that returned everyone to their own doorstep.

sections.name: Brains and Bronze
sections.subtitle: a dwarf reading his own dossier, and the archivist who wrote it
sections.overview:
The tablet's glow sat in [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik)'s beard like a small blue weather system, and he was reading. Not skimming. Reading, with one thick finger under the line, the way a man reads a contract he intends to sign.

I know what he was reading, because I wrote it. Volume eleven. The Deldkur dossier. The passage where I described the dwarf as *brains and bronze* and meant it as a compliment with an edge on it, the way all my compliments are issued.

He got to the phrase. His finger stopped. He read it twice.

"Brains and bronze," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said, out loud, to the room.

I have been in a great many rooms. I have been in throne rooms, count-houses, three separate courts, and one collapsing mirror. I have never been in a room where somebody read my work in front of me and I did not know what to do with my hands.

"That's mine," I said. "That's a Waluigi original. You are reading a *Waluigi original*."

"I know." He did not look up. "It's good. It's — accurate."

Something happened in my chest that I am contractually obliged to describe as indigestion.

"At least you're reading my articles," I said. "Someone has a brain, at least. Do you know how many people in this manor have opened volume eleven? Zero. The number is zero. I checked. I have a counter."

"I don't know much technology," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said, and finally looked up, and there was a smudge of mortar dust still on the tablet's corner from the wall they had all climbed the night before. "But I like reading."

"You *like reading*." I put both hands over my heart. "You had better get used to it. Because if we are doing things the right way, you are doing it my way, and my way is *documented*."

The dwarf smiled into his beard and went back to volume eleven, and for about four seconds the Overgrown Manor was the best posting I had ever held.
sections.waluigi_note: Forty volumes. Ten years. One reader, found in a hallway at an hour with no name, holding the tablet at the angle men hold things they intend to finish. I will not be recovering from this. I will be mentioning it in every filing until somebody asks me to stop.

sections.name: Not My Library
sections.subtitle: the thing at the end of the room, and what it was eating
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) looked to his left, which is the sort of small ordinary motion the archive is obliged to record because of everything that came after it.

A guy was eating something. That was the first reading. A figure at the far end of the reading floor, hunched over, working at something with the patient rhythm of a man at a long meal.

Then the shape resolved. It was not a guy. It was a shambling mound — a wet green haystack the size of a cart, standing in [the Overgrown Library](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/overgrown_library) among the bare joists and the coiling roots, and what it was eating was *books*.

Not the shelves. Not the librarian rooted into the west wall with his golden-red canopy and his bough arms. The books. It took them off the low racks one at a time, unhurried, the way a cow works a hedge, and the sound they made going in was the sound of a boot in deep mud.

[the Veteran](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_veteran_fairy) came up off [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik)'s shoulder and got altitude in one bent-winged lurch, hung there, and saw it.

"It's eating the books," he said.

"Not my library," said [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik).

He said it flatly, the way another man says *not today*, and the archive wishes to note the possessive. It is not his library. He has been in it twice. He was nearly killed in it once, by a bookshelf, in an incident I have filed and will not be discussing. He said *my* anyway.

The mound turned a fraction, and a page came out of the side of its mouth and hung there, browning.

"How hurt is it?" [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said.

Nobody knew. That is worth writing down plainly, because everything that followed was built on it: they could not tell. A shambling mound at full health and a shambling mound three-quarters dead look identical from a doorway. It was wet, it was green, it was chewing.

"We could go around," [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) offered.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) was already unslinging the warhammer.

"We're taking the room back," he said.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* The standing order was UPSTAIRS. The main room, the prince, the plan we spent a whole night and one tactical map building. He threw it over for a room full of paper because something was chewing it. I want that on the record before the part where it works.

sections.name: As You Said in Your Waluipedia
sections.subtitle: the marching order, and a war nobody has heard of
sections.overview:
"We need strategy," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said, and then, turning, with the delivery of a man producing a citation: "As you said in your Waluipedia. I love strategy."

Reader. He *cited* me. Mid-corridor. To a fairy.

[the Veteran](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_veteran_fairy) came down onto the reading rail and folded the good wing. "We can take him."

"Seems like you lot are decent at stealth." [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) was already sorting them with his hands, the way he sorts everything, as though people were crates with a correct stacking order. "I'll decide marching order."

He pointed at the fairy.

"You. Veteran. First. Can you lead?"

And the small battered thing with one wing bent at an angle wings do not bend said, without any particular emphasis:

"I fought wars in Barckelhaven. Not one person died. I can lead."

Nobody in that corridor had heard of Barckelhaven. I have forty volumes and Barckelhaven is in none of them. I wrote the name down twice, once phonetically, and I want to draw attention to the credential he chose. Not a rank. Not a battle. Not a body count in the useful direction. *Not one person died.* That is what he offered as proof of competence, and [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) — who has spent this entire campaign trying to get people to stop dying — hired him on the spot.

"Then the fairy," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said, "then me, then [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee)."

"Tree guys," he added, meaning the mounds.

[Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee)'s head came up. "*Three* guys?"

"No. *Tree* guys."

"Oh." A pause. "Okay."

I stepped forward at this juncture, because the running order was wrong.

"Stay with your audience, little toad," I said, moving smoothly into the second position, which was mine by right of magnificence. "Let me show you how a REAL show happens."

[Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) went third. He did not argue. He walked up to [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik)'s side instead, and the two of them looked at each other and nodded, once, the way people do when they have stopped needing the sentence.
sections.waluigi_note: *Waluigi files the marching order as evidence.* The dwarf put the unknown fairy at the front because the fairy asked, and asking is the only credential this house has ever respected. Barckelhaven remains unverified. Pending a second source, the archive holds the name and not the war.

sections.name: On Three
sections.subtitle: a distracted stationary target, and the overkill that followed
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) leaned to me and put it under his breath, close enough that I could smell mortar dust and old ale.

"On three."

They went in low along the joists, and the stealth was — I will be honest, because the archive is not a place for flattery — genuinely good. Four beings crossing a floor with no floor in it, stepping joist to joist, and the mound did not turn. It had a book. It was busy.

Then [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) swung, and missed.

A warhammer going through empty air makes a specific noise, a kind of disappointed *whoomph*, and it was followed by the small private silence of a dwarf recalculating. He swung again. He hit. The mound came apart at the shoulder like wet thatch.

"How," I said, with feeling, "do you MISS a distracted stationary target?"

"It moved."

"It did not move. It was *reading*."

Then the goblin staff arrived, because the manor's servants have developed the habit of appearing wherever violence is already underway, and they ran up the joists in a loose green wave and stabbed it. Repeatedly. With the enthusiasm of people who have wanted to stab something in this house for weeks and have finally been handed a target that cannot report them.

And I raised one magnificent hand and put a magic missile into the centre of the mass.

It exploded.

I want to be clear about the sequence, because I was proud of the missile for approximately one second before the arithmetic caught up. The mound was already coming apart when I cast. The goblins had already opened it. [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik)'s second swing had already taken the shoulder off. It was a wet green ruin held together by habit, and I detonated it, and it fell.

It was overkill. It was, in fact, the third or fourth kill of the same creature, and the archive suspects it was well on its way to dead before anybody in this party looked at it.

The pieces steamed on the joists. A half-eaten book lay open in the wreckage, pages down.

"Well," said [the Veteran](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_veteran_fairy), from above, "that's that."

The tree librarian at the west wall did not say anything at all.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* Four attackers, one dying shrub, one exploded. The party will tell this story as a victory and the story will be true and the story will also be a lie, and the difference between those two things is the entire subject of the argument we had ninety minutes later.
sections.imageCaption: The second swing, the one that connected. Goblin staff already up the joists with spears; the missile leaving Waluigi's hand; Toad Lee third in the order with the axe he would afterwards be unable to account for. The Veteran holds altitude on a bent wing. Four attackers on a creature the fey residents had already half killed.

sections.name: The Yew Leaf and the Pointy Stick
sections.subtitle: looting a shrub, and a question asked twice
sections.overview:
[Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) started picking at the corpse immediately, which is a habit the archive has stopped commenting on and started budgeting for.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) pulled a yew leaf out of his component pouch — flat, waxy, dark, the kind of thing that costs nothing and is impossible to buy in a hurry — and held it up between two fingers. Then he took the mound's own weapon out of the wreckage: a length of hardwood, sharpened at one end by nothing more sophisticated than growth.

A pointy stick. Now a sword.

He turned it in the lantern light and looked satisfied in a way I have only otherwise seen when he is being underpaid.

Then he reached over and patted his man on the back.

"That was not that hard, right?"

Silence.

"Sorry — what was that?" said [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee).

He had not been listening. He had not, as far as the archive can establish, been *present* for a measurable portion of the fight. He was standing over a corpse he had personally been picking at, holding an axe, and the question arrived at him from a long way off.

I wrote it down. I did not say anything. I wrote it down.

This is the third time. There was the missing time before Morel's warning. There was *I swung out of instinct* in the corridor with the leaf. Now there is a Toad who came out of a stealth engagement and had to ask what the sentence was.

"If we stealth like this," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said, delighted, oblivious, "we can do anything."

He flipped the warhammer.

The warhammer did not come back down into his hand. It came down onto the floorboards about four inches from his own boot with a bang that went all the way up into the roots, and every goblin on the joists flinched.

"Oh...." He picked it up. "Sorry about that."

"I want more action," said [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee), to nobody.

"I know," I said. "You're the action toad."

"I still want to be safe with [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik)," he said, and there was nothing in his face at all when he said it.
sections.waluigi_note: *Waluigi is not enjoying this section.* Three instances now: the missing hours, the instinct swing, and a question asked twice over a corpse. Filed under ANCHORS, drawer one, alongside Morel's warning. The archive does not believe in flukes and has stopped pretending to.

sections.name: Renown, Favour, and the Newspaper Club
sections.subtitle: two treants, a job offer, and a lost dog
sections.overview:
They went back toward the planning room, opened the door, and stopped.

The room was in open battle. Two treants — actual treants, thirty feet of arguing timber apiece — and shambling mounds among them, and the manor's people in the middle of it in a chaos that had gone past tactics and into weather. Furniture was airborne. Something was on fire in a corner and nobody had the time.

"If we fight these two shambling mounds," [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) said, thinking out loud, fast, "we can gain renown. Favour in the manor." He turned to [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik). "Maybe they can help you get back to [Archie](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser)."

And I saw the opening and I took it, because I am what I am.

"Or," I said, "forget [Archie](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/archie_miser)."

[Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) blinked.

"Join my newspaper club." I spread my hands to indicate the scale of the offer, which was considerable. "Write stories. For me. You have an eye — you notice things, you pick at corpses, that is ninety percent of journalism. I will give you a byline. I will give you *two* bylines."

"No thanks," said [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik).

"I did not ask *you*."

"Our best bet," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) continued, entirely untroubled, "is to gang up on one of the plant monsters."

He moved off to take the room from the side. And I stopped [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) on the way past, because the question had been sitting in me since the marching order and it came out with more edge on it than I intended.

"You going to follow him like a lost dog?"

[Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) did not rise to it. He looked at me for a moment with those flat dark eyes.

"I'm not a pet," he said. "I just think he is reliable."

Then he went after the dwarf.

I was annoyed. I am recording that I was annoyed, and I am recording that the annoyance was not about the Toad, and I am not going to elaborate further at this point in the filing.

"Come on, boys," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) called from the doorway.

We went up to the door.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* I offered a Toad a career and he chose a dwarf. I have made worse pitches to better prospects and closed them. The difference is that my club has a byline and a printing schedule, and {HJ} has never once left anybody in a room he could have left them in.

sections.name: The Hallways Are in Surprisingly Good Shape
sections.subtitle: polished marble, warm light, and a house being eaten
sections.overview:
The archive is going to slow down here, because the corridor deserves it and because of what it means.

The hallways of the fey manor are in surprisingly good shape overall, with rather minimal wear or damage. The plaster is cracked in places. The wood has seen better days. Everything is clean, and polished as well as it can be.

A vast carpet runs in all directions, well worn from the footsteps of countless beings, but clean — and it rests upon polished marble that is equally worn and equally well cared for.

Warm light fills the hallways from numerous glowing glass orb lanterns affixed to the walls.

Now hold that against everything else in this filing. There is a shambling mound eating the library. There are two treants in the planning room. There is something in the kitchen that ate a person, and a Revel downstairs that has been playing the same reel for weeks, and an overgrowth coming up through the floors of a house that has been dying by inches since before we arrived.

And somebody is still polishing the marble.

Somebody is still trimming the lanterns. Somebody walked this carpet with a brush this week, in a war, while the walls were producing vines, and got the dust out of a rug that has been walked flat by a thousand years of feet.

I have audited institutions in collapse. I know what a failing house looks like from the inside: the accounts stop first, then the maintenance, then the staff, and the last thing to go is always the lie that everything is fine. This house has done it in the opposite order. The staff are dying. The accounts are a map with pins in it. And the lanterns are *warm*.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) walked down the middle of that carpet with a warhammer over his shoulder and did not remark on any of it.

I remarked on all of it, silently, at length, and filed it under the heading the archive has been circling for three sessions now: the Overgrown Manor is not a house losing a war. It is a house *keeping standards* during one, which is a different and much sadder thing.
sections.waluigi_note: *Waluigi's professional opinion:* you can measure a household's morale by the objects nobody is required to care about. The marble is polished. The lanterns are lit. Whatever else is true of this house, its staff have not yet agreed to let it look like what it is.
sections.imageCaption: The corridor, unretouched. Plaster cracked, panelling tired, carpet walked threadbare down its centre line by a thousand years of feet - and clean, on marble that has been polished this week. Every lantern is lit. Note the vine at the left, already through the wall. Somebody is still keeping standards in a house being eaten.

sections.name: The Creation in Them Ate Someone
sections.subtitle: two guards holding a door, and the name they said first
sections.overview:
Two guards were shutting a door. Not guarding it — *shutting* it, both shoulders, the way you close something that is pushing back.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) asked, reasonably, whether there was a way around it. He wanted to flank.

"The creation in them ate someone," one of the guards said.

Everybody stopped.

"Wait." [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) put a hand flat on the door beside the man's shoulder. "You *saw* someone eat someone?"

They had. They did not want to describe it, and they described it anyway, in the compulsive way people do. Then the second guard jerked his chin further down the hall, toward the noise, and gave us the shape of the next room before we asked for it.

A battle was going on in the kitchen.

"There's a commander in there. [Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander)." He caught himself. "He — she. She's preparing the dinner."

"Dinner," I said.

"She will eat you alive." He said it with the flat conviction of a man repeating something he has been told and has never tested. "Like the monsters do. She's the heir's greatest soldier."

I would like the record to reflect that this is the second time in this house that a woman has been described to us before she was met, and that the first time the description was of a Lady and the reality was a plant wearing her face.

"We're both going to die on our own terms," the guard added, with a kind of exhausted gallantry.

"That's not the Hjumpik way," said [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik).

The guard looked at him.

"Huh? What's that?"

"My name."

And his friend — the other guard, the one who had been holding the door with his whole body — made a small strangled noise and went slightly to pieces, in the manner of a man whose reserves have been spent for some hours and who has just been handed one absurdity too many.

He got the door to the mushroom room open. Both of them went in.

They got drunk.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* The dwarf's entire personality is a load-bearing joke and he deploys it as a morale weapon. Two men holding a door against something that eats people, and he broke them with the etymology of his own name. It worked. That is the horrifying part. It WORKED.

sections.name: Danger Is My Middle Name
sections.subtitle: a bluff, delivered upward
sections.overview:
"Going up can be dangerous," one of them said from inside the mushroom room, in the loose confiding voice of a man who has recently discovered he has feelings.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) did not break stride.

"That's my middle name," he said. "Hjumpik *Danger* Deldkur."

I want to enter into the archive, formally and with citations, that this is not true.

The Deldkur line runs Piktor Deldkur the Third, deceased, one arm, great warrior; and before him a Second and a First that nobody in three planes has heard of and that I intend to find. There is no Danger in it. There is no Danger on any document, guild roll, contract, or bar tab I have ever seen the man sign, and I have seen a number of his bar tabs, because I have paid several of them.

He made it up. Standing in a corridor, at an hour with no name, in a house where the marble is polished and something in the kitchen eats people, a sober dwarf invented a middle name to make two frightened drunk guards feel better about a staircase.

The guards did not react. They were, at this point, extremely occupied with the mushroom room.

I reacted. I wrote *DANGER (invented, in situ)* in the margin and underlined it, and then I sat with the underline for a moment, because there is a version of that joke that is a man showing off and there is a version that is a man doing a job, and after four sessions in this manor I have stopped being able to tell them apart. He does the bit. The room gets lighter. Somebody who was about to stop moving keeps moving.

Forty volumes and I still do not know whether [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) is funny on purpose.

"Let's go," he said.

They left, and went upstairs.
sections.waluigi_note: *Waluigi, Auditor-General, certifies the following:* Hjumpik Deldkur has no middle name. He has a warhammer, a grandfather, a guild he will not name, and a habit of manufacturing exactly as much courage as a corridor requires. The invoice for that service has never once been issued.

sections.name: We're Here to Cook
sections.subtitle: the withering plant, the pot of slop, and the door with a key
sections.overview:
"Ow. Ow, ow." [Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander) was going at her work with the sound of somebody who has burned the same two fingers more than once this shift. She looked up. "Who are you? Did orange guy send you?"

The heir. Orange guy. The archive notes the manor's chain of command in four syllables.

"You're here to stop the plant monsters?" [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) asked.

"No. No." She waved the question off with a ladle. "We're here to *cook*." And then, with what I can only describe as professional satisfaction: "The plants love this."

She held up what she was making.

It withered in her hand.

Not wilted. *Withered* — went grey and slack between her fingers in about a second and a half, the green going out of it like heat out of a poker, and she watched it do that with the expression of a woman checking a sauce.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) got it before I did. I will admit that in writing. He looked at the grey thing in her fist and then at the pots and then at the doors the guards had been holding shut, and something reorganised behind his eyes.

The food is bad *on purpose*.

She is not defending the kitchen from the overgrowth. She is *provisioning* it. She is running poison out through the one system this house has never stopped operating — the service, the trays, the dinner — at the scale a great house does everything, and she is calling it dinner because that is what it is.

She handed [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) a pot of the slop. It smelled like a pond in August.

"You will stay for dessert," she told him. Not a question.

Something was wriggling in an oven. It was wriggling with intent, and it had a rhythm, and every single one of us decided independently and simultaneously not to ask.

"Maybe later," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said.

"...Wait." I had been reading the room, which is my function. "What's in that door?"

[Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander) produced a key from somewhere in the apron.

"Oh, this?" She turned it over. "Nothing much. A shortcut to the main room."

*Nothing much.*

I took her running sheet off the prep table on the way out, because I am what I am.

[[prop:prop_red_dinner_service_sheet|Open the kitchen's dinner service sheet as taken.]]
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* The best strategy in this manor belongs to the cook. Everyone upstairs has a map with pins in it. She has a service that already runs, a schedule the enemy already trusts, and a poison the enemy already eats. And the only direct route in the house is in her apron pocket.
sections.imageCaption: Red demonstrates the manor's best strategy: the plant goes grey and slack in her fist in about a second and a half. The pot she is handing Hjumpik is the same recipe at scale. Behind her the oven door is shut on something that was wriggling with intent, and nobody in the room asked about it.

sections.name: Field Observations
sections.subtitle: the guard who was fine, and the half hour he cannot account for
sections.overview:
A guard was telling anyone who would listen that the mushroom room had no effect on him whatsoever.

He was very clear about it. Unaffected. Completely fine. Sharp as a tack, in fact, sharper than usual, and he would thank you not to imply otherwise.

His eyes were bloodshot to the rim.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) noticed. I watched him notice — the small still moment, the beat where a dwarf decides not to say a thing — and then he asked, mildly, about the other one. The colleague. There had been two.

"Where did he go?"

"He's in the mushroom room." Cheerfully. "Want to see?"

We went and looked, because the archive goes and looks. The room was warm and low and smelled like a cellar in the good way. [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) crouched, picked up a mushroom, turned it over, and sniffed it.

Fine. Ordinary. A mushroom.

That is the part I cannot make fit, and I have been trying since. The mushrooms test clean. The men who spend time in the room do not. Something in there is having an effect that is not in the fungus, and the fungus is what everyone is looking at, and I have a horrible suspicion that this is the design.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) walked away, then turned around and went to the bathroom instead, which sounds like a joke and was in fact the single most productive decision of the night.

Later — after the bathroom, after the ash — he came back to [the mushroom room guard](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_mushroom_room_guard), and the missing colleague had returned, and the two of them had this exchange in front of us:

"Hey. The mushrooms didn't have any effects."

"Oh." A pause of exactly the wrong length. "I didn't think you would come back that soon."

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik): "Where were you?"

"Field observations."

Field observations. Two words, in a corridor, from a man with a hidden door behind him.
sections.waluigi_note: *Waluigi flags the sentence, not the mushroom.* "I didn't think you would come back that soon" is not the language of a man who was somewhere innocent. It is the language of a man who had a window and misjudged it. The fungus is a decoy and I will be filing on this again.

sections.name: Fifteen Minutes at the Bathroom Door
sections.subtitle: a lady with no face, one spark, and something in the toilet
sections.overview:
There was a guard outside the bathroom, standing at parade rest, and he informed us with real pride that he was guarding the lady of the manor.

"You have been here for fifteen minutes," said [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee).

The guard's face did something complicated.

"What? She said twenty minutes ago—"

"What did the lady look like?"

"She was hiding her face."

Nobody said anything for a moment. In the walls, faintly, the vines ticked.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) knocked. Then opened the door.

A plant monster came out of the bathroom.

And I would like the archive to note that I did not hesitate, deliberate, or consult. A spark of fire left my hand before the thing had finished emerging — not one of my larger works, a small precise unkind one — and it went into the centre of the mass where a heart would be if the thing had bothered with one.

It turned to ash. All of it, at once, standing up, and then not standing up.

Nobody had guarded a lady. A guard had stood at a door for fifteen or twenty minutes protecting the privacy of a thing that was hiding its face because it did not have one, and he had been *proud* of it, and I have no joke for that.

We investigated the room. And in the toilet, I found something.

"Is it poop?" [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) asked, from the doorway, with the directness that makes him such a poor diplomat and such an excellent witness.

It was not. It was a violet fungus — squat, purple, unmistakably alive, and regarding us.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) crouched to its level.

"Do you speak English?"

The fungus did not.

He turned to me. "Can you translate this?"

"*Huh?*" I drew myself up. "I am a field archivist, not a translator."

"Maybe Waluipedia has it."

And he pulled the tablet out, right there, crouched over a toilet in a fey manor at two in the morning, and started searching my encyclopedia for a violet fungus phrasebook.

"I'll be right back," he said, and went to find the guards.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH!* He looked it up. In the middle of an operation, over a talking mushroom in a toilet, the dwarf consulted the archive as a working reference. That is what it is FOR. Forty volumes and its first field deployment is a fungus in the plumbing. I have never been prouder or more insulted.

sections.name: Three Knocks, and a Circle
sections.subtitle: the credentials, the passage, and where it went
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) went back to [the mushroom room guard](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/the_mushroom_room_guard). A secret hatch opened somewhere behind the panelling, and the missing colleague came back through it, and we had the *field observations* exchange the archive has already filed.

Then [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) asked the only question that mattered.

"Why should we trust you?"

The guard held up fingers. Three of them. He had them ready, which is itself a finding.

One. [Aurelian](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/lady_aurelian) is helping.

Two. [Orangus Cornelius](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/orangus_cornelius).

Three — and here he warmed up, and leaned in, and became briefly the hero of his own account — "I stopped [Wario](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/wario). Actually, I did quite a bit."

Let us take these in order. The first is a woman currently folded into a gold ring in [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik)'s pocket, who has helped nobody in some weeks. The second is a name the guards of this house have refused to say out loud since the sitting room, delivered here as a *reference*. The third is a claim made by a very large number of people, almost all of whom are lying, and none of whom have ever produced a receipt.

[[prop:prop_mushroom_guard_three_credentials|Open the three credentials as transcribed.]]

"Fine," said [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik).

The guard knocked three times. A door opened in a wall that had no door in it.

I note, without comment, that [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) had been given the instructions first, had tried it himself, and had failed. Three knocks. He got it wrong. The house does not open for people who have been told how; it opens for people it knows.

The passage was one-being-wide. We went in single file — wall on both shoulders, the smell of dust and old plaster, somebody's lantern throwing our shadows forward in a long jointed row — and we scurried through it with the particular indignity of important people in a crawlspace.

There were others in there. Waiting. In the dark. They did not explain themselves and we did not ask.

And then the passage let us out.

Back where we started.

All of us. The whole party, the guards, the waiting figures, out into the same stretch of corridor we had entered from, with the same warm lantern light on the same well-cared-for marble.

That is when I stopped being able to do this politely.
sections.waluigi_note: *Waluigi's structural note.* A secret passage that returns you to your own doorstep is not a fault in the house. It is the house's opinion, expressed in architecture, of everyone currently walking around inside it. We have been in this manor for weeks and it has decided we are furniture.

sections.name: I Can't Afford Not to Care Anymore
sections.subtitle: the argument, the door Waluigi opened, and the hand that tried to stop him
sections.overview:
"You know what," I said. "We have been going in circles. And we are *losing*."

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) turned around.

"Look at how many people we have lost to your incompetence," I said, and I did not stop, because it had been building since the marching order and the lost-dog remark and the fungus in the toilet. "And that Toad too - he just sits around and follows you. At least the fey in this house *care* about it."

"We killed one of the big plant monsters," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said. "Right?"

"A half-dead one. That was almost killed by the fey residents before we got there."

"Do you want to just run around and fight things," he said, "or think before you act?"

And here is where I want the archive to slow down, because the argument turns over on this line and I am the one who turned it.

"Thinking has led us this far," I said. "We're not dead. But if we don't act, they reach the heir, and we are stuck with the plants forever."

"No. No, no." [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) put a hand out - not at me, at the corridor, at the whole green length of it. "We can't fight every battle. *Look at these guys.*"

"I one-shot that shrub almost ten minutes ago."

"Remember the goblins stabbed it and it died." The dwarf's voice went flat in a way I had not heard from him before. "I don't think that's saying much."

Which was true. Which is exactly the point I had made myself, in this same corridor, about this same shrub, and which I now needed not to be true.

"Then if they're that weak," I said, "we should take them on."

And I opened the door.

I want that recorded in the active voice, because I have spent this entire filing recording other people's decisions and this one was mine. Not the dwarf's. Mine. His hand came up as I reached past him - too slow, or slow on purpose, or slow because he had spent the night being told by me that thinking was what was killing us - and it closed on the air where my sleeve had been.

The monster was standing in the middle of the room, surrounded by people. It was not half dead. Nothing about it was half dead. It turned its whole mass toward the doorway, found us in it, and roared, and the sound went through the polished marble and up into the warm lantern light and out into a house that has been keeping its standards for a thousand years.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) looked at me. Not at the thing in the room. At me.

"Since when did you care?"

And I heard myself answer, in the corridor, over the noise, before I had cleared it with any part of myself that handles policy:

"I can't afford not to care anymore."

The Revel played on downstairs. The filing ends here, in a doorway I opened, mid-roar.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Read the transcript back and the whole argument inverts on one line: the dwarf was the one saying we cannot fight every battle. I was the one who said take them on, and then reached past his hand and opened the door. Ten years of filings and I have never written that sentence down. I have written AROUND it. Next filing begins in that doorway, and it is mine.

aftermath:
The library is held and nobody is holding it. The party retook a room, looted a corpse for a pointy stick, and walked out of it toward the planning room without leaving a guard, which means the reclamation is currently a sentence in this filing rather than a fact on the ground.

Three threads leave this session open. The first is Red: she has a working counter-strategy, an operating supply line, and a key to the main room, and nobody has yet asked her the obvious question, which is whether the heir knows what she is cooking. The second is the mushroom room, where the fungus tests clean and the men do not, and where a guard misjudged how long he had. The third is Toad Lee, who has now lost time in combat three times, and whose "I still want to be safe with Hjumpik" was delivered with nothing at all behind the eyes.

The violet fungus is uncatalogued and untranslated. The circular passage has not been re-entered. And the standing order - upstairs, the main room, the heir, the plan built on a tactical map over a whole night - has now been abandoned for a full session and replaced with nothing.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The victory was not one, and I used that against him and then against myself.** A shambling mound already fought by the fey residents, then stabbed by a goblin staff, then hit by a warhammer, then detonated by me, is not a trophy. It is a queue. I said so, and I was right. Then Hjumpik said *we can't fight every battle* - the dwarf, the one who hjumps on things, counselling restraint at me - and I answered *if they're that weak we should take them on*, which is the exact reasoning that gets parties killed, and which I had disproved myself ninety seconds earlier. He put a hand out. I opened the door anyway. The thing behind it was not weak at all. The archive records that the Auditor-General won the argument on the facts and lost it on the only question that mattered.

**2. Hjumpik abandoned a night's planning for a room full of books and it was the right call.** *Not my library.* Three words, no deliberation. The archive has spent four sessions watching this house treat every room as a corridor to somewhere better, and the dwarf is the first person in it to defend a place because it was worth defending. It cost us the upstairs plan. File it as a loss in the ledger and a gain in every other column.

**3. The cook is winning and nobody upstairs knows.** Red has what the war room does not: a delivery system the enemy already trusts. The heir has pins. She has a poison the overgrowth eats voluntarily, at scale, on a schedule. If this manor survives, it will not be because of the sixth and seventh divisions. It will be because somebody kept making dinner. RECOMMENDATION: get her a second cook and get out of her way.

**4. Toad Lee, third instance.** The missing hours. *I swung out of instinct.* And now a question asked twice over a body he was looting. Three is not a pattern the archive can keep calling a coincidence, and Morel's warning about anchors was specific. Somebody needs to sit down with him while he is definitely himself, and somebody needs to decide what we do if that stops being a thing we can schedule.

**5. The passage went in a circle and the house meant it.** Three knocks the dwarf was taught and could not reproduce. Others already waiting in the dark. Everyone deposited back on their own doorstep. This house has a functioning hidden infrastructure that opens for its own people and returns strangers to where they started, and we have been walking around inside it for weeks congratulating ourselves on our stealth.

**6. On the sentence.** I said I could not afford not to care anymore. I said it in a corridor, over a roar, to a dwarf who had just asked me since when - and he asked it *because* I had spent the whole night telling him caution was killing us and had then opened a door to prove it. The question was not rhetorical. It was a man looking at somebody who had just behaved completely out of character and asking, reasonably, what had changed. What changed was volume eleven, and a finger under the line. RECOMMENDATION: none. There is no recommendation. WAH.
