title: I Can't Afford Not to Care Anymore: The Doorway, the Colour Division, and the Lady Who Answered to Carnivorous
date: 2 Aethel, 922 BF (Feyward clock) - continuing without a break from the doorway Waluigi opened at the close of the library reclamation
era: Raventree Crisis - Feyward Operations / The Manor Fracture / Mages' Guild Retrieval
location: The Overgrown Manor - the Revel room doorway, the green corridor, the hallway post, the kitchen, the lower locked room, the upper landing, and the lady's sealed sanctuary
type: Feyward Party Fracture / Special Forces Retrieval / Boss Confrontation
summary: The door Waluigi opened at the end of the last filing turned out to contain a treant at full height, a Revel that could no longer tell which of its own members it was fighting, and no way for anybody to read how damaged anything was. Hjumpik dragged Waluigi out by the sleeve and the two of them had the argument the arc has been building to - glory against arithmetic, theatre against survival - and settled it on an exchange rate rather than an agreement. Then a Toad missed a bomb throw, a veteran picked it up, a treant made another treant, and somebody finally asked whether wood burns. Downstairs, a hallway guard reported that the manor's dead reinforcements had sword slashes and not plant wounds, and suggested loading the kitchen's poison into a bomb. Red changed out of a bugbear-demon shape behind a closed door and came back human, reporting the trees. Behind a locked door on the same floor, four Iron Legion special forces operatives introduced themselves by colour, identified Hjumpik by his wolf-pelt onesie, and took Toad Lee and Waluigi as leverage against an overdue contract. Hjumpik bought ten minutes, read two paragraphs of the Autumnwood Accords under duress, and walked into the lady's sanctuary alone, where the vines shut the doors behind him. The thing wearing Lady Aurelian explained its whole plan - collapse the manor, grow trees in the ruin, the beauty of nature is slow - and then said the word carnivorous and answered to it as a name. Hjumpik threw Red's poisoned dinner into its chest. The glamour came apart, the floor opened, and the session ends with a dwarf at a locked bathroom door, a satyr losing a fight behind him, and the Mages' Guild beating on the door in front.
description: Waluigi files this one as the session where the archive's own commentator stopped being able to pretend he was outside the story. He opened the door. He said out loud, in a corridor, that he could not afford not to care any more, and then spent the rest of the night being dragged out of rooms by a dwarf doing arithmetic he could not argue with. It is also the session where three separate institutions finally showed their hands at once: the Revel, which cannot tell its own members from its enemies and spent forty-four turns proving it; the Iron Legion's Colour Division, which crossed a planar boundary to collect one overdue contractor and did it in ten efficient minutes; and the overgrowth itself, which turns out to have a name, a timetable, and a stated preference for doing this slowly. In between there is a missed bomb throw, a guard nobody has relieved holding the only real clue in the building, a kitchen commander who changed species between two lines of dialogue, and the first person in a week to ask whether trees are weak to fire.

sections.name: I Can't Afford Not to Care Anymore
sections.subtitle: the sentence that opened the door, and the thing on the other side of it
sections.overview:
I ended the last filing in a doorway and I am going to begin this one in the same doorway, because nothing about it improved in the interval.

The door was open because I opened it. [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik)'s hand closed on air. Inside the room was the Revel, and the Revel was not alone, and the thing standing in the middle of the floor was a treant with its full height under it — not the half-dead shrub I had been using as a rhetorical device for the last twenty minutes of corridor. It turned. The floor took the weight.

*I can't afford not to care anymore.* I said that. It is filed. I stand by the sentence and I would like the record to note that I said it approximately four seconds before the sentence became expensive.

Behind me [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) had the axe out and was looking at the thing with an expression I could not read, which is normal, and [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) was already doing arithmetic, which is worse.

What neither of them said out loud, and what the Revel's fey said for them in the same breath, is the part this filing has to answer: **some of the people in that room were not fighting the tree. Some of them were fighting for it.** The Revel has been a party for three sessions. It has now produced combatants on both sides of the same floor, and nobody in the manor can tell you which fey is which until it swings.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Read the last filing's final line and then read this one's first line. Same doorway, four seconds apart, and the entire cost of the sentence lands in the gap. I have never been so pleased to have written something down and so unhappy to have meant it.

sections.name: He Cannot Tell How Damaged It Is
sections.subtitle: the dwarf's assessment, and the reason he stopped making one
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) looked at the treant for what I will generously call three seconds and then said, flatly, that this did not look really good and was kind of pointless.

I want to be fair to him in a way that I was not fair to him in the corridor, so here is the actual problem he had, in his own terms: **he could not tell how damaged it was.** Bark does not bleed where you can see it. A treant with forty hit points left and a treant with a hundred and forty look identical from a doorway. In the library, the mound was visibly half-eaten, and that visible half-deadness was the entire basis of my argument that these things are weak. Here there was nothing to read.

So he did the thing he does, which is stop assessing and start moving.

"I'm going to drag [Waluigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/waluigi) out of this," he announced, to nobody, and then did.

I would like the archive to understand that I was not carried. I was *pulled*. There is a difference and it is the only dignity available to me in this section.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* He is right that you cannot read a treant's health from a doorway. He is wrong that this makes fighting it pointless. It makes fighting it UNKNOWN, which is a different word, and the difference between those two words is the entire argument this session is about.
sections.imageCaption: The doorway, resolved. Hjumpik with both hands on the sleeve, hauling; Waluigi braced across the frame with his arms out, refusing to be hauled; Toad Lee third with the axe, looking back at a treant at full height and the second one budding beside it. The dwarf's whole strategy in one grip.

sections.name: It's Not an Ambush If It's Right Here
sections.subtitle: the spirits shouting about the plan, and the dwarf who would not fight a stranger
sections.overview:
The Revel's spirits objected immediately and at volume.

*Wait — our plan, the ambush — where are you going?*

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) did not break stride. "It's not an ambush if it's right here. So... unless you know how strong this guy is, I won't fight them."

*Ugh,* said the Revel.

I want that exchange preserved exactly as it happened, because it is the first time in this arc that somebody has said the quiet mechanical thing out loud. An ambush is a fight you chose. A fight in a doorway you happened to open is a fight the room chose. [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) will take the first one all day and will not take the second one at any price, and the Revel — which planned the ambush, which has been planning the ambush for two sessions — could not follow the distinction fast enough to argue with it.

Meanwhile I was still being towed.

"Why are you pulling me away from the action?"

"Well, there's a giant tree you ran into the room with. I'm trying to save your life. *Strategy.*"
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* "It's not an ambush if it's right here." Write that on the war room wall. The fey have spent two sessions building a trap and cannot recognise that a trap you fall into yourself is just a hole.

sections.name: Think of the Glory, Think of the Manor
sections.subtitle: the argument in the hallway, at volume, again
sections.overview:
"Bah. I hear you." I did hear him. Hearing him has never once stopped me. "But think of it — the *glory*. Think about the manor. We have been running away for so long. What's the point? This manor will collapse."

"You pick your fights," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said.

And there it was. The dwarf's entire philosophy, four words, delivered like a door closing.

"You pick your fights? Then why are we in this mess?" I did not lower my voice and I am not going to pretend I did. "Because you let someone get away. Because you took inaction. That guy ran away — and you *healed* him into a giant plant. I'm tired of running. [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) follows you like a giant stub."

He let me go.

Not dramatically. He just opened his hand, and my sleeve came back, and the two of us stood in a hallway in a house that is being eaten, having said the true things.

"What should we do, then?" he said. "Since you love fighting — I'll follow what you say, and see if you're right."

"I have been leading you guys. What do you think, Mr Bossman?"
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* He handed me the command and I handed it straight back, and neither of us wanted it, and that is the most honest thing this party has done all week. The archive files a leadership dispute resolved by mutual refusal.

sections.name: We Need Something Theatrical
sections.subtitle: a bomb placed in a Toad's hand, and the veteran who picked it up
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) pointed at [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) and put a bomb in his hand.

Not *gave*. Pointed first, then placed. The Toad looked at the bomb. The bomb, one of Wario's, looked at nobody.

"We need something theatrical," I said, because we did. ""[Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee)— throw the bomb."

He threw the bomb.

He missed.

The bomb was picked up by the House Guard veteran, and from there the evening stopped having a shape. A guard holding a live Bob-omb in a corridor full of fey who cannot agree which side they are on is not a tactical situation, it is a *category error*, and the room resolved it the way rooms do.

"You're a deserter," somebody shouted at [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik). "Deserters get killed."

"You didn't say you'd fight this battle — you're attacking *me*? **Attack the tree.**"

"Well, I guess it's, uh — there's a bomb in there, and people started going crazy. And now there's TWO. They're multiplying. That's not good."

A guard, helpfully: *it's stronger than you three combined.*

The treant animated a second treant. [Waluigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/waluigi) — me — stood there stone-faced while a tree made another tree out of a room I had personally insisted we enter.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* I asked for theatre. I received theatre. The archive notes that the request and the disaster were separated by one failed throw, and that I have no grounds to complain about either, and complains anyway.

sections.name: Are These Guys Weak to Fire Damage
sections.subtitle: the only useful question asked in the whole engagement
sections.overview:
"Are these guys weak to fire damage?"

"They're wood, so probably."

That is the entire exchange. It took four seconds. It is, on the evidence of this session, the single most productive conversation the party has had since the kitchen, and I want it filed with the same weight the archive gives to a treaty.

Because here is the thing nobody in this manor has done: **nobody has tested the vegetation for the obvious weakness.** Not the household, which has been stabbing it. Not the guards, who have been shooting it with crossbows at a hundred feet. Not the Revel, which has been putting it to sleep. Not us, and we are the ones with a fire mage in the party roster and a kitchen downstairs that produces poison by the stockpot.

A house has been under siege by wood for a week and the first person to say the word *fire* out loud said it in a corridor while retreating.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Wood. Fire. Two of them, in a house, in the Feyward, for a week. I am going to be thinking about this section for a long time and none of the thoughts are flattering to anybody present, me included.

sections.name: Put Your Own Theatrics Into It
sections.subtitle: a compromise between strategy and showmanship, negotiated mid-retreat
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) decided to help the people upstairs. He said it out loud in the shape of a sales pitch, which is new for him: "I'll do that. That's, ummm — win-win. I'll help you, and I'll take out more tree monsters."

"Let's go find the others. *Strategy*, right?"

I told him I like theatre more than strategy.

And he said the thing that ended the argument, and I am filing it as the most competent piece of man-management I have witnessed in this campaign:

**"Put your own theatrics into it. So we don't die, and you get your theatrics."**

"Okay. For now. I still want that thing dead. If you run away, I'll stay and fight."

That is where we left it. Not agreement. A rate of exchange.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* He did not tell me to stop wanting the spectacle. He told me to route the spectacle through the survival. I have been managed. I noticed at the time and I allowed it, which I maintain is a different thing from being managed.

sections.name: They Had Sword Slashes
sections.subtitle: the hallway guard, the dead reinforcements, and the detail nobody followed up
sections.overview:
The same reinforcements guard was standing in the hallway. He said he had been guarding the hallway. He has, as far as this archive can establish, been guarding the hallway this entire time.

"What happened to the reinforcements?"

"They died."

"From the plants?"

"**Not from plants. From other people. They had sword slashes.**"

I want a straight line drawn under that and I want it drawn in a colour the reader cannot ignore.

The overgrowth does not carry swords. The treants club and throw bark. The violet fungus rots. The shambling mound engulfs. Every single casualty this house has taken from vegetation has looked like vegetation did it. These did not. Somebody with an edged weapon killed the manor's reinforcements in a corridor while the household's entire attention was pointed at the trees, and the only person who noticed was a guard nobody has relieved and nobody has debriefed.

Then he offered the best idea anybody has had in this house: put [Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander)'s soup in a bomb.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik): "We need a bomb specialist."

Me: "Oh. Wario is one."

And that is where the thread stops, because nobody in this party has yet done the arithmetic where the poisoned dinner and the explosive meet.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Sword slashes. SWORD SLASHES. I have filed three sessions of this manor's plant problem and one sentence from a man who was not invited to any of the planning has just put a second enemy in the building. Nobody followed it up. I am following it up. It is a lead and it has a file number now.

sections.name: The Coins, the Shadow, and the Satyr
sections.subtitle: a summoning in a hallway, and the thing from the toilet
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) shook his coins.

A shadow arrived. It walked up the hall toward us and resolved, as it came, into the purple thing from the bathroom — the violet fungus, the one from the toilet, the one we left in there because there was a more interesting door.

The satyr killed it.

I am filing the whole encounter in three sentences because it took about that long, and because the notable thing is not the fungus. The notable thing is that [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) has a way of shaking coins that brings something to him, that what it brought was a satyr who fights on our side, and that nobody at the table asked him a single question about it.

He wanted to go upstairs. He had, by his own account, been *swayed* to come over here instead.

"Let's see what the lady wants," he said, and we went to the kitchen.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* The dwarf shook a purse and a competent swordsman appeared. I have known him for three sessions. I am filing an open question rather than a guess, which the reader should understand costs me something.

sections.name: All Women Here
sections.subtitle: a closed door, a change of clothes, and a commander who is not what she was
sections.overview:
[Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander) wanted the door closed. She needed to change; she had got her clothes dirty.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik): "Why?"

"I need privacy."

"But you have cooks in there."

"We're all women here."

The door closed.

The door opened.

And [Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander) was human. Not a red bugbear demon — a woman, standing in her own kitchen doorway with flour on her hands, in the same coat.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik): "Who are you?"

"No, no — it's *me*. The trees are multiplying."

I have read this exchange back four times looking for the seam and I cannot find one. The archive's position, filed plainly: **the manor's kitchen commander changed species behind a closed door and gave no account of it, and the first thing she said on the other side was about the trees.** She was not hiding. She was reporting.

"We need an actual solution," [Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander) said. "How did this happen?"

"From a guy with mushrooms growing on him."

"We need to take it out at the source."

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik): "I didn't want to kill an innocent."

[Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander): "Sometimes we have to kill for the greater good."

There is a whole political philosophy in that exchange and neither party noticed they were having it.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* She changed shape and reported the tactical situation in the same breath, in that order, and the archive would like to know which of those two things she considered the news.
sections.imageCaption: The kitchen doorway, the moment after. Red out of the bugbear-demon shape and in a human one, hands still floury, mid-sentence and already back onto the trees. Hjumpik with his question half-raised. Waluigi in the doorframe, declining to be surprised on the record. The stockpot behind them is still going.

sections.name: I'm Red, and I'm Green, and I'm Yellow, and I'm Black
sections.subtitle: four operatives behind a locked door, and the onesie that gave the game away
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) tried a door. Locked. [Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander) said there had been fighting in there — slashing sounds — and that she had opened it after the plants left, and then a hand—

He asked to check it. She agreed to unlock it.

Three guards stood there. Then the magical girl sequence started.

*I'm Red.* *And I'm Green.* *And I'm Yellow.* *And I'm Black* — and the fourth one turned into a shadow.

"Like a black person, or—"

"Okay, so there are monsters over here. Have you fought any?"

"Yeah, we got the monsters. This goblin guy and demon guy." A satyr, for the record.

"Who are you guys? You don't look like guards here."

"We're part of the Colour Division."

"Colour Division?"

"Special forces."

"For who?"

"The Iron Legionaries. We were sent here to look for a dwarf named **Hjumpoo**."

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) — standing there, in the room, being looked at — said: "Hjumpik, you stupid."

"Why?"

"He took longer than five nights. His time's up. They want him back for the mission."

"I can relay that information to him."

"Really?"

And then Black said it. "Hey — you ARE Hjumpik. You have the signature wolf-pelt onesie on."

"Uhh, you know, a lot of dwarves use this stuff. It's kinda racist. *All* dwarves use wolf pelt."

He closed the door slowly and ran upstairs.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Four special forces operatives crossed a planar boundary into a house full of carnivorous architecture to collect one contractor, and the identification was made on a garment. Not a description, not a sigil, not a writ. The onesie. He has been wearing the onesie for three sessions and I have never once thought of it as evidence.

sections.name: By the Order of the Lady of the House
sections.subtitle: a chase up a staircase, and a guard post argued past in nine words
sections.overview:
He looked below during the chase. They were coming.

At the top, the house guard held the line the way the house guard always holds the line: "By the order of the Lady of the House, you can't go in."

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik): "What if she's a fake?"

Nothing. The guards held.

"I don't have time. If you close the door, bring us in — we can talk."

"Fine. Fine."

The guards stood down. Everybody ran in. The Legion arrived at the door behind them and started banging on it.

*By the order of the Legion, open the door.*

"Alright, listen — keep this quick. People downstairs are getting killed by the trees."

And then [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) looked around the room and stopped.

**The other tree battles are gone.** This was the same room where he and I used the freezing spell. The frozen statues. The engagement we left in progress.

Empty.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* "What if she's a fake?" — asked as a delaying tactic, by a man who does not yet know he is going to be right about it within the hour. I have filed a lot of accidental prophecy in this archive and this is the cheapest and the best.

sections.name: A House Divided Against Itself
sections.subtitle: the theory session, conducted at speed, with a door being beaten on
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) had questions and the Legion had a battering fist, so he asked them fast.

"Say the plant monster wanted to take out the lady of the manor, but couldn't. To get this manor, you destroy the manor or take control of the leader — common sense. Let's say this plant monster wanted to take control of the lady, but she couldn't. **So what if they changed into the lady themselves? Can we rule that out?**"

"But we've been winning some battles, right? We cleared all these rooms. Why would a plant want to remove other plants from itself?"

"Good question. I don't have a complete answer. Why were we struggling, but now we're not?"

I put in: "What if the fake lady wanted to control the manor from the *outside*?"

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik): "A house divided against itself can't stand. Why would they kill themselves to hide themselves?"

"Well — it could be a vengeful spirit."

"Could be. But doesn't make sense."

"You were there when the fake one fought us."

"No, no — maybe they realised they can't beat us."

"But they *were* beating us. Continuously."

"What I'm saying is: something's fishy and I don't like it. These guards are chasing me."

"Just keep your eyes open. We're losing and they're retreating. **Use your brain.**"

[Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee), who had said nothing for two sessions: "Maybe an ambush."

"Yeah. Maybe. Maybe an ambush, actually."
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Toad Lee spoke twice this session and was right the second time, which is a better hit rate than mine. The archive would like it noted that the correct answer to the whole theory session was supplied by the party member I described, in a corridor, ninety minutes earlier, as a giant stub. I retract nothing and I record everything.

sections.name: Five Months
sections.subtitle: the guards' account of their watch, and the arithmetic Hjumpik did out loud
sections.overview:
"What happened recently?"

The guard's account, filed as given: "Well, we were at the hot spa, and we planned a push. So we killed some tree monsters and cut some leaves. But by the time we reached this room, we found some frozen statues in here and no plants to be seen. Soon the Lady returned. She asked us to guard the room while she does some preparation to kill the plants. So we have been doing that."

"No one else came in or out?"

"We're guards."

"Sure."

And then [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) did the arithmetic.

He has been in this house for three months. He said it out loud, and then he kept going, and the number moved.

*Five months.*

He looked at his cowbell. He recalled his past. He relearned it — that is the only verb available and I am using it under protest. I waved my hand in front of his face and got nothing. No reaction. The dwarf stood in a guarded room with the Legion beating on the door below and an unaccounted-for two months arriving in his head all at once.

For the record, I want the archive to hold three facts next to each other and not resolve them:

1. The Lady asked the guards to hold this room while she *prepares to kill the plants*.
2. Nobody has come in or out, because they are guards.
3. Hjumpik has lost two months he did not know he had lost.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* The cowbell again. Second session running it has done something to him and second session running nobody has picked it up and looked at it. I am putting it in the investigation file whether he likes it or not.

sections.name: Leverage
sections.subtitle: the ambush that was actually an ambush, and the price of ten more minutes
sections.overview:
The stair doors burst open. The Colour Division came through.

They apprehended [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) and [Waluigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/waluigi) promptly and without theatre, which I resented.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik): "You got me. I'm Hjumpik."

He thought about asking for more time. He decided against asking for time, and asked for something narrower instead: "No, I don't want to get any time. Just let me investigate first."

"Well — YOU can. But your friends there are apprehended right now."

"Why don't you just want me? Why them, in the crossfire?"

"**Leverage.**"

I did not want to kill the Mages' Guild. I want that filed, because the option was available and I considered it and the consideration was brief but it was real. Still...

"You know what — fine. Sure. I'll see what's in this room."

"Wait. Please read this."

And they handed a dwarf, in a corridor, mid-siege, [[prop:prop_accords_900_20_containment|six pages of the Autumnwood Accords on containment-zone maintenance]].

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik), having read it: "You want me to monitor this place?"

"No. That's what *we* are tasked to do."

Then they read him the part that actually applied — [[prop:prop_aegis_magi_recall_clause|the Recall clause]]. *In the event that a bound object flees its designated location, the Aegis Magi may be authorized to track and retrieve it using Recall magic, the costs of which shall be borne by the owner.* Collateral that can walk away requires extraordinary security.

"Your mission is over, Hjumpik. You failed."

"You said it was simple. Look what happened. Plants came. Other stuff. No flak."

"Well — what have you achieved? Something *tangible*?"

"I'm getting to the bottom of this place."

"Anything tangible to show the Aegis Magi, and maybe they'll hold off a bit."

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) clutched the ring in his pocket. The one with Aurelian in it.

"How about this. Since you've got me cornered — I'll just check the room over there. I'll come back out. Hold me back for a bit."

"We want something, then. Insurance. Give us one item."

"You have my friends. You're lucky I'm not blasting you guys."

"Fine. Go get the mage cages."

"No — no mage cages." [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) had the warhammer in his hand without appearing to have picked it up. "No cages. They're not animals. Just hold them."

"Fine."

He produced handcuffs.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) signalled to me to escape if things got bad. I slipped the handcuffs immediately and stood there wearing them anyway, because there is no theatre in an empty cuff.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* They read him the regulations. In a corridor. During a siege. Six pages on containment-zone maintenance and then one paragraph about retrieving property that walks away, and only the second document was actually about him. That is how an institution tells you what you are without using the word.
sections.imageCaption: The landing, the moment the leverage was named. Toad Lee held between Red and Green; Waluigi cuffed and unbothered, having already slipped them; Yellow and Black at the stair door. Hjumpik alone in the foreground with a hand on the warhammer, buying ten minutes with a ring he has not shown them.

sections.name: Yes, Yes, Come In
sections.subtitle: the door that closed behind them, and the thing that was pleased to see them
sections.overview:
He opened the door gently.

"Ready to go, [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik)," said the satyr from earlier, who had been there the whole time.

"Sure. Why not."

They took a step in.

The doors closed. Vines locked them.

*"Yes, yes — come in,"* said Aurelian. *"We need to talk."*

"Yeah.... sure."

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) went forward. **"Come face me."**

Then, one step later, out loud, to the room: "Wait — why did I come in here? Actually, this was a horrible idea."

The vines covered every door. The full room was crawling. He walked over anyway.

"Who are you?"

"I'm the one that will rule the manor."

"You're collapsing this place."

"Yes. And once it collapses, trees will grow anew."

"Then why impersonate the lady?"

"I needed to move some puzzle pieces. Put them into place."

"Why not just — why waste our time? Go out and kill everyone."

"Well. The beauty of nature is *slow*." A pause. "Have you smelt the fungus spores yet?"
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* It answered every question. Every single one. A monster with a complete plan, a stated objective, and the patience to explain both — and the only reason we got the explanation is that it had already won the room and could afford the conversation.

sections.name: That's... My Name
sections.subtitle: a question about furniture, asked twice, and a bowl of dinner
sections.overview:
[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) looked at what it was sitting on.

"Since we're dying anyway — what plant are you sitting on?"

"Oh, this? Sadly, it's just a foflower."

"Is it?"

"Yes."

"Ever wondered if sitting on this is bad for plants?"

He took another step. "You sure?"

"Hmmm. What do you mean?"

He smirked. "Are you sure that plant is good to sit on? Plants are *carnivorous*, right—"

And it said: **"That's.... my name....."**

I have transcribed that with the pauses in because the pauses are the evidence. Something in the thing wearing Aurelian's face heard the word and answered it as though it had been addressed. Not *plants are carnivorous, yes*. Not a correction. A name, given, by accident, in the middle of being condescended to about furniture.

"I have something for you," [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) said. "Since it's my last day — why don't I give you something special?"

He threw the food right at her.

[Red](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/red_the_kitchen_commander)'s dinner. The poison that withers the overgrowth in the hand. Straight into the chest of the thing that runs it.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* He killed a monster's composure with a question about seating. Then he threw soup at it. I have been arguing for two sessions that this party needs to be more theatrical and the dwarf who hates theatre just out-staged me with a bowl.

sections.name: The Show Can Begin
sections.subtitle: the glamour ending, the floor opening, and a bell rung in a corridor
sections.overview:
It was damaged.

Damaged is not beaten. Its eyes started bleeding, and then the black came, and then the plants came out of the eyes. The mouth went hollow and kept going, past where a mouth stops. [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) — who has walked into a treant's reach twice this session without changing expression — was horrified, and the archive is recording that because he is not a man who is horrified on paper.

The floor opened.

*"The show can begin."*

The satyr ran at it. "I'll stop this." He failed horribly.

The plants on the floor shrieked.

[Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) rang the bell.

Aurelian glowed orange, and her eyes rolled back. The ring in his pocket glowed. And the satyr stood there.

I do not know what happened. I want that in writing, in my own voice, in an archive I control: **I do not know what happened.** A cowbell, an orange glow, a soul ring, a monster mid-transformation and a satyr standing perfectly still in the middle of it.

Then [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) ran — away from her, directly into the violet fungus. He jumped one. Barely cleared it. Reached the locked bathroom door.

The bathroom was locked.

The satyr is locked in a fight he did not pick, behind him. The Mages' Guild is beating on the door, in front of him. The floor is open in the room he just left, and something with roots where its eyes were is currently deciding what to grow into.

The filing ends with a dwarf between two doors, both of them shut.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Last session ended in a doorway I opened. This one ends at a door that will not open, with the same dwarf on the wrong side of it, and me in handcuffs I have already escaped from one floor down. Somebody is going to have to admit that this house has a pattern.
sections.imageCaption: The sanctuary room, after the bowl. The glamour is finished: black down the cheeks, shoots out of the sockets, the mouth open past where a mouth stops, Red's slop steaming down the gown and blackening the petals. The floor is already splitting. Hjumpik is turning to run with the cowbell up and ringing.

sections.name: The Ledger — Three Rounds, Forty-Four Turns, Nothing Decided
sections.subtitle: what the combat log actually says, translated out of dice
sections.overview:
The engagement in the Revel room ran three rounds, forty-four NPC turns, twenty-four attack actions and thirteen spells, and produced **no decision whatsoever.** Most of the fighting was a standstill. I have the ledger and I am going to read it honestly, which means reading it against us.

**Busiest combatant: the Satyr Swordfighter** — eight multiattacks, and its focus was the House Guard. Not the treant. The *House Guard*. A fey swordsman spent the entire engagement attacking the manor's own soldiers.

**Most-targeted: the Treant** — which sounds like progress until you count who was doing the targeting. The House Guard put six multiattacks into it with heavy crossbows. The Satyr Bard cast Sleep at it three times. The Sprite Caster cast Sleep at the Wyght. The Satyr Sorcerer spent four spells on the *Satyr Swordfighter*, which is to say the Revel spent its magic fighting itself.

**The tally by hand:** Satyr Swordfighter 8 multiattacks, focused House Guard. House Guard 6 multiattacks, focused Treant. Satyr Sorcerer 4 spells, focused Satyr Swordfighter. A Satyr: 3 attacks and 2 spells, focused [Waluigi](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/waluigi). Satyr Bard 3 spells, focused Treant. Treant: 1 multiattack, 1 spell, focused Satyr. Goblin Line Cook 4 attacks, focused Satyr Swordfighter — and healing itself between throws off packets of questionable powder it calls *seasoning*. Satyr Druid 1 attack, 1 spell. Satyr Rogue 1 multiattack, focused Satyr Bard. Sprite Caster 1 spell. A second Treant, 1 spell. Red Scullion: no actions. Shambling Mound: no actions, incapacitated.

**What the numbers mean, in plain terms.** The Revel is not a faction. It is a room full of individuals who have not agreed on an enemy. A rogue emptied a hand crossbow and two shortswords into a bard on its own side. A sorcerer put Colour Spray into a cone containing a treant and a druid. A druid Thunderwaved a swordfighter. The house's own guards put crossbow bolts into [Toad Lee](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/toad_lee) and into [Hjumpik](https://mikegent01.github.io/bik/index.html#/article/hjumpik) — [[prop:prop_revel_engagement_ledger|nineteen points of damage across four bolts]], logged, against the two party members who were not attacking anybody.

The Treant, meanwhile, cast Animate Trees twice. It is not fighting a battle. It is *reproducing* in the middle of one, and the only reason the number of treants is not higher is that the room ran out of rounds before it ran out of trees.

And the sleeping one died. That is the last line in the log and I am giving it its own paragraph because somebody in that room went down asleep, under an enchantment cast by an ally, and the log does not say who cast the last blow.
sections.waluigi_note: *WAH.* Forty-four turns and the most effective combatant in the room spent all eight of its actions on the wrong side. This is not a battle report. It is a diagnosis, and the diagnosis is that the Revel cannot tell friend from enemy any more — which, given that we have spent this session establishing that the lady of the house is a plant, may not be a failure of discipline at all. It may be the correct reading of the room.

outcome: No room was taken and no enemy was beaten, and the party's position is materially worse than it was at the start of the night. The treant in the Revel room was not fought; it animated a second treant and the engagement dissolved into a three-round standstill in which the Revel's own members did most of the damage to each other. Toad Lee and Waluigi are in Colour Division custody as leverage against Hjumpik's overdue Aegis Magi contract - handcuffs rather than mage cages, on Hjumpik's insistence, and Waluigi slipped his immediately and is wearing them by choice. Hjumpik traded an investigation window for that custody and spent it walking alone into the lady's sanctuary. What was gained is information, and it is substantial: the overgrowth's objective is stated (collapse the manor, grow trees in the ruin), its patience is explained (the beauty of nature is slow), its impersonation of the lady is confirmed as deliberate piece-moving, and it answered to the name Carnivorous. Red's kitchen poison works on it at range, thrown by hand. The manor's dead reinforcements were killed with edged weapons, not vegetation, which puts a second hostile party in the building that nobody has accounted for. And Hjumpik's own reckoning of how long he has been in this house moved from three months to five in the middle of a sentence.

"It's not an ambush if it's right here" - Hjumpik's refusal to fight an unread enemy
"Put your own theatrics into it. So we don't die, and you get your theatrics" - the compromise that ended the argument
"Are these guys weak to fire damage?" "They're wood, so probably." - the first fire test proposed in a week-long siege against vegetation
"Not from plants. From other people. They had sword slashes." - a second killer in the manor, reported by a guard nobody debriefed
The Colour Division: "I'm Red. And I'm Green. And I'm Yellow. And I'm Black" - the fourth turns into a shadow
Hjumpik identified by his wolf-pelt onesie, and his defence that all dwarves use wolf pelt
"Leverage." - one word, and the party has two hostages in it
Three months becomes five months, mid-monologue, in front of a cowbell
"Plants are carnivorous, right-" "That's.... my name....."

reputationNotes.hjumpik: His Aegis Magi engagement was declared failed and over; the Division took two of his people as leverage against the overdue contract, and he refused to surrender the only asset that would have satisfied them.
reputationNotes.waluigi: Taken into Colour Division custody as leverage, was out of the cuffs before anybody noticed, and has not mentioned it.
reputationNotes._record: A Mages' Guild contract failed publicly and the Colour Division took hostages over it — cuffs rather than mage cages, agreed without argument, which is the part worth filing.

aftermath:
**Standing.** Nothing in the Overgrown Manor is held. The Revel room contains at least two treants and a fey faction that spent three rounds unable to agree on a target. The lady's sanctuary has an open floor in it and something in the middle of finishing its transformation. The corridor between them is unguarded, as every corridor in this house has been since the first filing.

**Custody.** Toad Lee and Waluigi are held by the Colour Division on the upper landing, cuffed, as leverage. The cuffs are cuffs and not mage cages because Hjumpik put a hand on a warhammer and said they are not animals; the Division agreed without argument, which should worry the reader more than a refusal would have. Waluigi is out of his and has not mentioned it.

**Contract.** Hjumpik's Aegis Magi engagement is declared failed and over. The Division wants one tangible item as insurance against the window he negotiated. He has the soul ring with Lady Aurelian in it in his pocket and did not offer it, and the archive notes that the only asset he has that would satisfy them is the only asset he will not surrender.

**Open threads.** The sword slashes on the manor's dead reinforcements are unexplained and unpursued. The soup-in-a-bomb proposal has a supplier (Red), a specialist named (Wario), and no bomb. The fire question was asked and never tested. The two missing months in Hjumpik's reckoning have no account attached. And the thing in the sanctuary answered to Carnivorous, which means the archive now has a name for the overgrowth and no idea what holds the name.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. I opened the door and the bill arrived immediately.** I spent the last filing arguing that these plants are weak and that thinking is what has been killing us. I opened a door on that argument and found a treant at full height, a room that could not be read, and a dwarf who told me - correctly - that you cannot assess a thing you cannot see the damage on. I was pulled out of that room by the sleeve. The archive will record that I was not grateful at the time and that I am, in writing, now.

**2. The argument was settled by a rate of exchange, not by anybody being right.** *Put your own theatrics into it, so we don't die and you get your theatrics.* That is not a concession, it is a currency conversion, and it is the most competent thing Hjumpik has done in this campaign. I have been managed. I noticed at the time. I allowed it.

**3. The most important sentence of the night was said by a man nobody has relieved.** Sword slashes. Not plants. The manor has been fighting vegetation for a week with its entire attention, and its own dead are turning up with edged wounds, and the witness is a guard standing in a hallway waiting for orders that are not coming. I have filed that as a lead. If the next session does not pull that thread I will pull it myself and I will be insufferable about it.

**4. Forty-four turns of a faction fighting itself is not a battle report, it is a diagnosis.** The Revel's best swordsman spent eight multiattacks on the house guard. Its sorcerer spent four spells on its own swordfighter. Its rogue emptied three attacks into its own bard. Either the Revel has lost cohesion entirely, or - and I want this considered seriously - some of them are being controlled, and the ones fighting the house are the ones already taken. Given what we learned upstairs about who has been wearing the lady's face, I am no longer confident that a fey attacking another fey is a mistake.

**5. The Colour Division was the only professional organisation in the building.** They stated their objective, identified their target by a garment, took hostages they called insurance, granted a window they intend to close, and read a dwarf two paragraphs of regulation in the middle of a siege. Nothing they did was cruel. Everything they did worked. I file institutions I cannot outmanoeuvre with a particular kind of loathing and this is that entry.

**6. Hjumpik killed a monster's composure with a question about furniture, and then threw soup at it.** *Are you sure that plant is good to sit on? Plants are carnivorous, right—* *That's.... my name.....* I have spent three sessions demanding that this party be more theatrical. The dwarf who hates theatre out-staged me with a bowl of kitchen slop and a question about seating, and the archive is obliged to say so.

**7. Two months are missing and nobody has looked for them.** Three months became five months in the middle of his own sentence, in front of a cowbell that has now done something inexplicable in two consecutive filings, while I waved a hand in his face and got nothing back. He is the party's strategist and his own timeline has a hole in it. That is not a character note. That is a security problem.

location: The Overgrown Manor — Colour Division Quarters, Lady's Inner Sanctum, Servant Common Room, and the Goblin Card Room
summary: Toad Lee awakens from a daydream of his father to find himself tied in overgrown quarters beside an uncuffed Waluigi. After learning their guards are the Iron Legion's Colour Division, they confront Quartermaster Cornburary before Toad Lee's emotional surge triggers a torrential Feywild wildfire. Meanwhile, Hjumpik proposes to Lady Aurelia with a soul ring to break her power, losing his trousers in the scuffle before dragging her to safety. Guided by Brad the waiter, the party navigates a rotted common room to the goblin card room, where Brad reveals the Feywild will be severed in twenty-one days.
description: Waluigi files this one as the session where Toad Lee woke up from a daydream of his father with an axe to find himself tied in an overgrown bedroom, where Quartermaster Cornburary claimed to have shadow writers, and where Hjumpik dropped to one knee, proposed to Lady Aurelia, and promptly lost his pants. In between, Toad Lee proved that Feywild weather reacts to personal fury—unleashing thunder, hail, and wildfire upon the Iron Legion—while Brad the waiter guided the party past a rotted two-story drop to the goblin card room, where dirty cleaning supplies were wagered and the twenty-one day destruction of the plane was spoken out loud.

sections.name: A Scene of Wild Overgrowth
sections.subtitle: the daydream of an axe, the unlocked cuffs, and the story got mostly right
sections.overview:
Toad Lee wakes up full of expression, still tied up in the room.

A scene of wild overgrowth unfolds before you. Where once was a rather spacious living quarters, now the space is filled with twisting and coiling roots and vines. Soft green moss and clover grows in through the seams of the floor, its invasion bringing subtle bits of green to an otherwise very brown room.

Of the numerous windows that line the walls of this large room only a few of them let light filter in, the rest having overgrown with vines.

The room features a large wardrobe, a fine writing deck and a four post bed that's taken on a life of its own. The rest of the space appears to be worn and water damaged but structurally sound.

He comes to his senses. He snaps out of it as if he was having a daydream throughout the majority of everything.

Toad Lee grunts up, walks around. Waluigi sits there, handcuffs still on but unlocked.

"Where am I, Waluigi? I was in a plain field with bright green grass, clear blue skies, there was a hill. I saw what seems to be my dad. We were play fighting. I was fighting with the axe I have, he was fighting with his? I don't know, I have some snippets of my father... ehh don't know."

"You want to go back?" Waluigi says.

"No, this is important. Remind me what happened."

"He offered us to see Aurelia. He sold us out."

"That can't be. Was he backed into a corner?"

"Well, we could have fought them, but I guess he was in a corner, they were chasing us." Waluigi walks to the chair. "There was a bunch of guards chasing us. Hjumpik wanted to see Aurelia. He gave us up because he had no choice, or because of selfishness."

"Maybe, I'm not sure."

The guards say he got the story mostly right.

"Sorry my sirs, didn't mean to," Toad Lee says. "While I wait for rescue, might as well look around."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. He woke up dreaming of play fighting his father on a grassy hill with axes, and within twenty seconds he had to process unlocked handcuffs, an overgrown four-post bed, and the fact that our dwarf traded us for an audience with a plant. I gave him the honest version: Hjumpik either had no choice or did it out of selfishness, and the guards agreed with my arithmetic.

sections.name: The Books in Elven and the Colour Division
sections.subtitle: the writing desk, the wrong denizens, and the leverage plan
sections.overview:
The few books sitting on or slipped into this writing desk's shelves are mostly journals, logbooks, and references. They are all written in elven.

Toad Lee asks for paper and a pen from Waluigi. Waluigi hands him his writing kit.

Toad Lee asks the guards if they can speak elvish.

"What? We don't know that."

"What do you mean you don't know this? Weren't you guys denizens of the Feywild?"

"Huh? We're the Colour Division of the Iron Legion."

"Wa?" Toad Lee says.

"We were sent here to capture Hjumpik. We needed you guys as leverage, and our plan is working. Once Aurelia beats up Hjumpik, we grab him and drag him out."

"You're very confident that will happen, aren't you?"

"Yes we are, as we are of Mr. Miser."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. He asked the guards if they speak elvish because we are in a fairy manor, and they looked at him like he had insulted their mothers. Special forces. The Colour Division. They don't speak elvish, they don't care about the flora, and they brought handcuffs because a dwarf owes hours on a contract.

sections.name: A Better Archivist Than Your Friend
sections.subtitle: Quartermaster Cornburary enters, the tennis racket threat, and shadow writers
sections.overview:
Quartermaster Cornburary enters the room. He smiles: "Yes, yes, our plans are well."

"Who are you?" Toad Lee asks.

"Cornburary."

"Cornburary of the Legion... you don't have a weapon on you. Are you a combatant here like your guards?"

"Is that a threat? Go ahead, hit me, see what happens."

"No, it's not a threat, I'm just asking."

"No, no, I don't need to get rough. I need to get Hjumpik."

"I'm just asking you a question, man. Would you please answer my question?"

"I am a journalist."

"A journalist?"

"Well, not really. A bookkeeper, an archivist even. A better one than your friend over there."

Waluigi shouts: "WAH! I'll take you out!"

"You sure are confident of yourself, you sure you can take him on?" Toad Lee asks.

Cornburary smirks: "I don't need to. I have a bunch of shadow writers that will do it for me."

Waluigi gets his tennis racket. Toad Lee says: "No, no!" He swipes at his racket; Waluigi backs up.

"Friendly fire! You're threatening my livelihood!"

"Don't attack yet. I'm banged up, we're in a tricky situation, Waluigi. We can't afford making another rash decision. We don't know what's going on entirely. Have a little restraint for me please, if not for yourself. Who will archive... uhhh, me when I'm gone or something?" Toad Lee says.

"Well, I will outlast you. WAH, fine."

"I'll repay you somehow," Toad Lee says. "I assume they sent you in the Feywild to hunt down Archie as well?"

"Archie is secondary," they say.

"Hjumpik's dead, or—"

"No, no."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. A bureaucrat walked through the door with no weapon, looked at my writing kit, and told me he had shadow writers who could do my job better. I pulled the Phase Spider gut racket out. Toad Lee swiped at it and called it friendly fire! You do not threaten an archivist's livelihood in his own filing.

sections.name: You Look Ravishing Tonight
sections.subtitle: the ash of the satyr, the spiky ring, and the pants that fell down
sections.overview:
Shift to Hjumpik.

Aurelia touches the satyr, burns him, turns him to ash.

"It's a sham," Hjumpik says.

"Haven't you forgotten something important? This is my manor."

Hjumpik says: "I'm Hjumpik, so ho ho ho, I'm not afraid, and this isn't my manor."

"With one touch, you will be gone too." She walks closer over the dust.

He takes out the glowing ring. He points it towards her.

"Huh, is that wedding ring? You're proposing to me?"

"Do something," Hjumpik whispers to the ring.

Hjumpik gets on one knee: "You're right, I am proposing to you. Put on this ring, ignore everything I said before. You look ravishing tonight."

Lady Aurelia smiles, getting out a ring with a spike in it.

"In fey culture males put on the ring. We will be bound once you put it in. It will slowly suck your lifeforce," she says.

"Oh really, wow, that's terrifying. But will this save my friends? Will you stand down?"

"Yes, of course. I'll release this manor from my shackles and focus them on you."

"Wow, it's almost like we are married."

Hjumpik shows his ring finger up. He jams the soul ring onto her finger!

She says: "Yaoui Dhayemmn Dhwayelf!"

"You... you idiot!" She smiles, "I order you to take it off!"

Hjumpik uncontrollably takes her ring up. She falls, her power weakening. She grabs Hjumpik's pants—they fall!

Guards run in: "WHAT THE? WITH THE LADY? WE CAUGHT YOU WITH YOUR PANTS DOWN!"

"Let's go back to your friends, the toad and purple one. This will be in the report."

"I need to check on the lady with something," Hjumpik slashes vines to the bathroom door and drags the body inside with him.

They shout: "NOW YOU'RE GOING TO THE BATHROOM WITH HER? GET BACK HERE!"
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. Read the transcript! He got on one knee, told a plant demon she looked ravishing tonight, jammed a soul ring onto her hand, and lost his trousers to her dying grip. The Legion caught him pants-down and promised it would be in the official military report. I could not make this up if I had ten shadow writers.

sections.name: The Men in Silver and the Reactive Emotion
sections.subtitle: the elven book on feelings, the CCC syringe, and the slip out the window
sections.overview:
Cut to Toad Lee.

Toad Lee remembers something about the Feywild: the environment of the Feywild is reactive to a person's emotions.

"Mutsdoppms apnd yoput hopw mutsdoppms capn apffetct det fetywapdd" the book is said. Toad Lee looks over it.

"Yes, yes, my men in silver come in." Cordon Combat Chirurgeon comes in.

"We are the CCC. We have to come eliminate the Feywild. With this solution we can simply inject the plants killing them."

Toad Lee mutters: "Great, another egocentric character... Dang, I do have a question. Why do you want to destroy the Feywild?"

"It is unpure."

"Define unpure."

"It does not follow the natural way of life."

"If you're trying to control it, it will be hard. Why do you want to?"

"Because we can."

"Wow, you're power-hungry."

Quartermaster Cornburary says: "We're not greedy."

"Waluigi, check outside for any probes."

Waluigi smiles, says "Okay," and heads to the window.

Toad Lee says: "This place has land and leaders. I don't think people, natives, will appreciate you guys taking it over. Foreigners conquering planes."

"Such is the way of life. No one likes being conquered, but that is what we do."

"Really, that's the only reason?"

Waluigi slips out.

"Well, not the only reason. Because the material plane is cur—"

Quartermaster Cornburary says: "Shut up, you! Too much information!" They start arguing.

Toad Lee cuts in: "No, no, no, please continue! You're from the Legion, right? And that's an Iron Legion uniform that you're wearing. What's the logo of the Legion, your heraldry?"

"You trying to get information from me? You won't, not even from that birdbrain over there."

"Fine, but I'll find out later on. That big emblem is telling me otherwise. We have a friend in yellow that has been feeding us quadrants. You will meet more of us in the material plane."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. The CCC brought a syringe of weedkiller to prune a dimension because it is 'unpure' and 'because we can.' Toad Lee stalled them with heraldry questions while I slipped out the window to check for probes. Bureaucracy cannot handle a conversation where someone asks 'define unpure.'

sections.name: Thunder, Hail, and Fire Everywhere
sections.subtitle: the emotional climate surge, the burnt journals, and jumping out the window
sections.overview:
Toad Lee is getting a little angry. Then thunder, then rain, hail pouring—FIRE EVERYWHERE!

"What the... woah, woah!" as he feels heat.

"Huh, so it actually worked, holy heck!" Toad Lee says.

Toad Lee takes the books. Some of them are burnt; he takes some that are not burnt while leaving others that are not entirely burnt.

Toad Lee slowly reaches towards the window. It is open, and Waluigi is gone.

"What the dang," he whispers.

He escapes as well, not without saying: "Listen man, the Feywild is not the type of place you want to set up shop outside of your imperialistic tendencies. Leave the Feywild alone! It has people living inside of it, they won't be happy when they find denizens invading on their own. Be warned!"

With that, Toad Lee jumps out the window.
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. He read one page of an elven book about mushroom feelings and summoned a localized apocalypse out of his own irritation. Thunder, hail, and wildfire! He grabbed the books, gave an anti-imperialist speech to a burning room, and threw himself out a window. Spectacular form.

sections.name: The Ceilings and the Waiter Guy
sections.subtitle: the princess carry, the worm in the eye, and Brad's briefing on P.S.
sections.overview:
Cut to Hjumpik in the past, before the fire and craziness.

In the bathroom with Aurelia, he looks up at the ceiling. Same hole.

Hjumpik tosses Aurelia. She falls back into his arms. *Princess carrying,* Hjumpik thinks.

He tosses her again; she falls flat.

He uses his warhammer again; she lands on the second floor.

Hjumpik examines the lady. A worm comes out of her soulless eyes!

"Ugg, we got to get you to safety. Let's get out of here. I hope Waluigi knows what to do."

He opens a door. It hits something. He quickly goes back, tries another door, and peeks out. Brad stands there. He doesn't recognize him at first, but then does.

"Are you the waiter guy?"

"You're still alive? Thought you died back there."

"I don't die that easily. Just want to get out."

"Get out? Where? There's nowhere to go."

"Why you sound so down?"

"This place is too chaotic. We have to stabilize it somehow."

"We should stabilize it actually, right?"

"Listen, there's someone here... well, a bit of people. They're invaders. They call themselves the Iron Legion. I'm not sure what they want, but they've been encroaching, and it seems with the power vacuum they might want to kidnap and take the lady for themselves."

"Yeah, I know."

"Their commander, P.S., I think her name is, I don't know what it stands for. I think she's working with other legionnaires from the outside world. She is leading the Sunflower Division. I'm not sure what other division is, but they're cooperating and they seem to want to kill or at least take out the two people of this manor. You don't want to take them out, do you?"

"No... that's not my goal here. I just want to help, get out of there, do what I need to do."

"Good, good. Just this way."

Fire spouts from the ground!

"Aaah, what's going on?!"

He opens a door: "What's in that door?"

"The bathroom!"

"You have water on you, something that can dampen these flames at all?"

Hjumpik runs through the fire grabbing the other guy. He uses his dwarven healing skills to heal himself: "Whatever, I'm out."
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. The waiter survived! Brad, who was pouring tea while the house was being swallowed by roots, is now running counter-intelligence on the Sunflower Division. And Hjumpik tossed a countess into the ceiling twice, thought 'princess carry,' and then watched a worm crawl out of her eye.

sections.name: The Mage of Ice
sections.subtitle: the secret kept, the tapped shoulder, and putting out the flames
sections.overview:
Cut to Toad Lee.

Toad Lee says: "What I learned about this place works... Wait, Waluigi, where are you going? WALUIGI!"

He walks more.

"WALUIGI!"

He feels a tap on his shoulder.

"Hmm, what the... Waluigi, don't scare me like that! Why did you run off?"

"Well, because those people, I'm not sure who they are."

"People? Who exactly, from where?"

"That."

"What about the probe the CCC and bald guy mentioned? You see any of them?"

"Hmm, I did, I waved it off, it flew away, who knows where it went."

"I hear you. This fire... this fire, I'm not sure, but I think I'm the cause of it, believe it or not. How did I do it? I know the answer, I don't trust you."

"Don't trust ME? How can I archive the answer to my million of fans?"

"Because knowing you, you will unleash chaos for the sake of it or for your interest. And I don't know, I may not be closest with these Feywild people, but I think they're still people. So... sorry, can't trust you with this secret I know. You understand?"

"Archie would've invited me to his fireball party. Oh well."

"I'll be honest, we have been in this manor for quite some time. I want to regroup with Hjumpik, and I have questions for him. So I guess we regroup, have sessions and downtime, and we decide from there what we do. But I will say we are sitting ducks out here, let's just go back inside and take cover or something."

"Ah, fire," Toad Lee says. "How do we put out fire?"

"They don't call me writer or ice."

"Hmm, they call you that? First time I heard it."

"No worries, mage of ice, work your magic," Toad Lee says.

Waluigi steps into the room; all fire is gone.

"Oh, you really did work your magic!" Toad Lee says.

"Huh, I did... yeah, I did!" Waluigi says.
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. Toad Lee told me to my face that he won't trust me with the weather secret because I would 'unleash chaos for the sake of it.' Then he asked me how to put out the fire. I told him I am the Mage of Ice. I walked into the room, the flames went out, and I took full credit.

sections.name: We Won, But Not the War
sections.subtitle: the reunion, the exorcised demon, and the rotting servant common room
sections.overview:
"Hello," Hjumpik says.

Toad Lee says: "Glad to see you back, we're reunited. Did you sell us out to the Legion for Aurelia?"

Waluigi stays quiet.

"The Legion was trying to capture my—wait, wasn't Waluigi and Toad Lee about to get captured?" Hjumpik says.

"We're reunited," Toad Lee says. "Didn't even have to get in the fire, took damage for nothing. You will be a new man after 8 hours and such. So, is that Aurelia over there?"

"Took the demon out of her. She tried to fight me, I got the demon out... yeah."

"Oh, you removed the demon from her, I hear you," Toad Lee says. "We have Aurelia, she doesn't look too good... everything okay with her?"

"Yeah, I knocked—I didn't, I had to exorcise her."

"I hear you.... yeah... hmm... this guy's going to..."

"Sorry, what?"

Brad says: "Let's get a move on, you can talk while we move."

They all follow him.

Not much is left of this room. The floorboards have rotted away in places, revealing a steep drop down to the library gangways a floor below. For the less fortunate, there is a drop all the way down to the first floor. This must have been a servant's common room at some point, but it has been rendered uninhabitable.

He takes a book out of the bookshelf. It slides up; they walk in silence.
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. 'I had to exorcise her.' That is the official dwarf account of hitting a noblewoman with a warhammer until a worm crawled out of her eye. And then Brad walked us across rotted floorboards with a two-story drop to the library. The hospitality here never stops.

sections.name: Twenty-One Days: The End of the World
sections.subtitle: the goblin card room, the wagers of clothes, and the countdown
sections.overview:
They end up here.

This small room looks like a library exploded into it. The floor is cluttered with as many discarded books as there are huge mushrooms growing out of them.

The table in the center of the room is piled high with a messy stack of cards and is surrounded by a pack of surly goblins playing a rowdy game. Just observing for a moment tells you these games can get quite heated, and the wagers seem to be anything from cleaning supplies to their own clothing.

The same place Hjumpik played cards.

Waluigi says: "Are you sure this is a good idea?"

"Yeah, this is kinda where she went haywire," Hjumpik says. Hjumpik thinks he has his own intentions.

Toad Lee sees a look of determination in Brad's eyes—they're baggy, tired, roughed up, but set.

"If we leave her here, what are we going to do? What's the plan?"

"Not sure," Brad says. "You guys wanted to leave, right? Maybe find whoever wanted to help you leave and uhh just go... I guess. I'll handle it from here."

"Only you? What are you going to do, a push of wind will push you down," Hjumpik says.

"I'll... work something out."

"Hmmm, I still want to help the manor, it's a bit late," Hjumpik says.

"The three beasts of the manor still live... the Bramblyfly, the Revel... it was a complete failure, wasn't it?" Brad says.

"Actually the archivist died at least. How many other guys, are they winning or losing?" Hjumpik says.

"A lot of the plants went away when she got knocked out, but there is still overgrowth and hot spots. This is the Overgrown Manor after all."

"The Revel, the satyrs, did they run away? What's going on with them?" Hjumpik asks.

"Not sure, probably pushing forward with evacuating the whole manor."

"The Revel, what about him, the Revelmaster?"

"I don't know, I have no answers for your questions, I've just been doing my best."

"Cheer up brother, we're winning. That's not what a fighter would act like," Hjumpik says.

"We won, but not the war," Brad says.

"Alright, do something, don't run around like headless chicken."

"I want to get rid of the satyrs and the rebels and try my best or fail trying. I uhh eavesdropped earlier, you know that? They said they're cutting the Feywild in a few days right, or something? 21 days is that it... the end of the world."

"Oh... I see," Hjumpik says.
sections.waluigi_note: WAH. A room where goblins gamble their shirts over dirty cards, surrounded by mushrooms and ruined books. And a waiter with tired eyes looked us in the face and said the quiet part: twenty-one days until they sever the plane. The clock is running.

reputationNotes: House Corvinarus views Hjumpik's Soul-Ring pledge as an unprecedented act of chivalric honour, substantially warming relations with Lady Aurelia. The Iron Legion views the property destruction and defiance of Quartermaster Cornburary as an active breach of contract.
aftermath:
**Standing.** Lady Aurelia is unconscious and bound by the soul ring, stripped of her demonic overgrowth authority. The Overgrown Manor remains infested with residual brambles, but the central floral power has broken. The Revel and satyrs are in disorganized retreat or evacuation.

**Custody.** Toad Lee and Waluigi escaped the Colour Division holding room via the emotional wildfire. The Legion's leverage plan collapsed, though Quartermaster Cornburary and the Cordon Combat Chirurgeon remain active in the sector. Lady Aurelia is currently sheltered in the secret goblin card room under Brad's custody.

**The 21-Day Clock.** Brad confirmed that foreign forces intend to sever or prune the Feywild within twenty-one days. This establishes an irreversible operational deadline for all factions within the manor.

**Open threads.** The true identity and orders of Commander P.S. (Sunflower Division) remain uninvestigated. The surviving manor beasts (the Bramblyfly and the Revel remnants) are still active on the grounds. Toad Lee's elven research volumes on emotional climate remain in party possession.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The proposal was madness, but the mathematics held.** Hjumpik dropped to one knee, called a plant monster ravishing, and shoved a soul ring on her finger. It cost him his dignity and his trousers, but it broke her hold on the building. I have filed many reckless actions in this campaign; this is the only one that ended in a marriage proposal and a military report.

**2. Toad Lee is a walking planar detonator.** The Feywild reacts to emotional climate. Toad Lee got annoyed with a bureaucrat, and the house answered with thunder, hail, and wildfire. He gave an anti-imperialist speech and leapt out a window with a stack of elven books. If he learns to weaponize that temper deliberately, nobody in this house is safe.

**3. Cornburary's shadow writers are a personal insult.** A quartermaster with no sword told me he had an army of scribes who could out-write me. I pulled my Phase Spider racket. Toad Lee called it friendly fire. I am noting for the record that my livelihood was threatened and I showed immense professional restraint.

**4. The CCC represents pure institutional rot.** 'Why destroy the Feywild? Because it is unpure. Because we can.' They brought syringes to purge a dimension. That is not science or defense; it is bureaucratic arrogance with a silver badge.

**5. Brad the waiter is the only competent intelligence operative in the house.** While everyone else was swinging axes or losing their pants, the waiter identified Commander P.S., tracked the Sunflower Division, located a secret sliding bookshelf, and eavesdropped on the twenty-one day planar severance plan. Give that man a tip.

**6. I am the Mage of Ice.** Toad Lee asked how to extinguish a room on fire. I told him they call me writer or ice. I walked in, the fire went out, and I claimed every bit of the credit. History belongs to those who show up when the flames stop.

**7. The twenty-one day clock changes everything.** The goblins are gambling their laundry away while the sky is being prepared for a guillotine. Twenty-one days until the Feywild is severed. We came here looking for an escape; now we are racing a planetary deadline.
